3.0.s.en: (1) The surrender of all the lands

3.0.1.en: When the lands were seized with fear and terror of the great army of Holofernes, which destroyed every land it met, they sent messengers to Holofernes from the rest of the lands, among them the lands of Syria, that is, the Levant, which extends from Iraq to the Mediterranean and as far as distant lands such as Libya. All of them begged for his kindness and asked to submit to him.

3.1.1.en: The messengers said to Holofernes, "Our lands are ready to be enslaved to you and to King Nabuchodonosor, for this is better than that you should kill us and destroy our lands." This shows the extent of the weakness, despair and humiliation to which they had come, so they surrendered completely.

3.2.0.en: Lord of peace: a peaceful ruler who neither kills nor destroys.

3.2.1.en: In their surrender the messengers offered Holofernes their lands with all their cities, mountains and fields, and also their various possessions of cattle, goats, camels and horses. They delivered themselves to him as slaves, old and young, and declared their readiness to obey him in all his commands. Their only request was that he should not harm them and their lands, but leave them to live in peace, since they saw that his power could not be resisted.

3.2.2.en: Do not fear the terror and power of the devil, and do not surrender and become enslaved to him and to your lusts, and to the pressures of his wicked helpers around you in the world, for fear that you may die. Rather, be confident that death is a passing over to life, which is better than being humbled under the hand of the hard-hearted devil.

3.3.s.en: (2) Conscripting the men from the captured cities

3.3.0.en: So Holofernes advanced with his great army and came down upon all the lands that had sent to appease him, and took possession of them. He chose the young men and the strong men able to fight and added them to his army, so that he had supporters from the lands he had taken possession of, and the strength of his army increased.

3.3.1.en: Holofernes, who is a type of Satan, if you surrender to him, is not satisfied with this, but conscripts all your strength and your senses for evil, in order to lead others astray and cause them to stumble through you, for he is wicked and exploits everyone who submits to him and walks in his way.

3.4.s.en: (3) The welcome of the lands for Holofernes and his destruction of them

3.4.0.en: Pipes: plural of the pipe, a wind musical instrument.

3.4.1.en: The inhabitants of those lands tried to appease Holofernes, so their leaders came out with garlands of flowers, lamps and musical instruments, such as drums and pipes, welcoming him as a great ruler who would lead their lands and govern them in peace, hoping by this to win his kindness.

3.5.0.en: Unfortunately these peoples found nothing but cruelty, and he insisted on destroying not only their cities but also their fields and their forests, so that no source of life would remain to them, because the king's command was strict that he alone should be the only god of all these peoples. So he destroyed their temples and the sacred groves in which they held their worship, so that they would worship no god but Nabuchodonosor. This shows the extent of the domination and violence in Holofernes, for he did not want to take possession of their bodies, their cities and their property only, but also of their souls, so that they would submit to the worship of the king alone.

3.5.1.en: You cannot make peace with the devil or appease him, for he is determined to destroy your life. The one who offers you the pleasure of lust at the beginning suddenly turns into a mighty giant who wants to destroy your life, because he desires to be your god instead of God, and to dominate your soul, indeed all souls.

3.6.0.en: Syria of Sobal and Bamia: anciently called Aram, it lies west of the river Euphrates and was a strong kingdom at that time.

3.6.1.en: The Edomites: they dwelt in Mount Seir and are the descendants of Esau. These mountains lie south of the land of the Jews and extend from the south of the Dead Sea to the regions of Egypt.

3.6.2.en: Among the lands that Holofernes took possession of were the lands of Syria (the Levant) and the land of the Edomites, and he rested there for a month in a city called Geba, where he reorganized the ranks of his army and arranged its needs, in preparation for continuing his sweep and his conquest of the lands of the world.

3.6.3.en: I wish that you would examine yourself, in order to rearrange your life every day and every month, so that you renew your covenants with God, ask for His help and be strengthened with your spiritual weapons, and so defeat your enemies the demons.

3.6.4.en: The readiness of the Jews to fight the Assyrians. After the first three chapters displayed the power of the Assyrian army and its sweep through all the lands of the world, chapters 4-7 show the faith of the people of God, the power that is with them, and their readiness to face this great army, as a preparation for triumphing over it.

4.0.0.en: Their loins: the plural of the loin, the muscle of man's chest, which trembles when he is afraid.

4.0.1.en: When the Jews who dwelt in the southern kingdom, that is, the land of Judah, whose capital is Jerusalem, where the great temple of God is, heard and learned the news of the army of Holofernes and its sweep through all the cities through which it passed and its destruction of their gods, they feared that he would attack the temple of Jerusalem and destroy it, and they also feared for themselves. This is the feeling of the ordinary human being at the horror of terrifying news.

4.0.2.en: It is beautiful that they feared for the temple of God, for this shows their love and their attachment to God's dwelling in their midst and their bond with Him, although this fear of theirs shows the weakness of their faith, because God is able to defend His temple if they hold fast to Him.

4.1.0.en: Samaria: the region of Samaria extends from Judea in the south to Galilee in the north, and from the river Jordan in the east to near the Mediterranean Sea in the west. In this region lies the city of Samaria, which was the capital of the northern kingdom of the Jews until the days of the Assyrian attack with which we are dealing. This city lies northwest of Shechem at a distance of five and a half miles.

4.1.1.en: Jericho: a great city, five miles west of the river Jordan and seventeen miles northeast of Jerusalem. It was the first city that Joshua took possession of when he entered the land of Canaan after crossing the Jordan.

4.1.2.en: Eliakim, the high priest who dwelt in Jerusalem (v. 5), was considered at this time the civil head, because King Manasseh was imprisoned in Babylon for a short period. Eliakim is Joakim, who sent messages to the whole region of Samaria as far as Jericho in the south when he sensed the approach of the Assyrian army, so that they would prepare for war and place guards on the tops of the mountains to watch the armies coming from afar, because the one on the top of the mountain can easily strike with arrows anyone who approaches the foot of the mountain.

4.2.0.en: To complete the preparations for war, the children of Israel took care to make walls for the villages that had no walls, because the cities and some of the villages had strong walls. They also took care to gather the harvest of wheat and other grains, such as barley, and stored it in the cities, so that if any city was besieged there would be food inside enough for the people for a long time.

4.3.0.en: Esdraelon: a plain, or a great triangular valley, whose base is at the river Jordan and whose tip extends to near the Mediterranean Sea; it lies north of Samaria and south of Galilee.

4.3.1.en: The great plain: most likely the desert of the Arabian Peninsula, that is, present-day Saudi Arabia, which lies east of the river Jordan.

4.3.2.en: Dothan: a region located northwest of the plain of Esdraelon, that is, toward the Mediterranean.

4.3.5.en: The passages: narrow paths between the mountains, which sometimes admit only one person, or two.

4.3.6.en: The high priest Eliakim sent in particular to the lands surrounding the plain of Esdraelon and lying on the roads leading to Jerusalem, that they should be strict in guarding the tops of the mountains with trained soldiers, and likewise should guard the passages that lie between the mountains, and thus prevent the passage of any army trying to reach the holy city Jerusalem, in which the temple of God is.

4.4.0.en: The leaders of the cities and villages and all the people obeyed the commands of the high priest and carried out all his instructions.

4.4.1.en: It is important in the spiritual warfare that a person exert all his effort in guarding his thoughts and his senses, and in closing every gap through which the devil can enter, and in caring for his spiritual food, and in arming himself with all the spiritual weapons: prayers, fasts and spiritual readings, especially in the places and circumstances in which an attack from the devil is expected, relying on his basic spiritual food, that is, partaking of the Body and Blood of the Lord.

4.5.1.en: Alongside the preparation for war, the more important thing was the spiritual work, so the whole people came forward not only with prayers but with crying and supplications to God, joined with fasting, to humble themselves before God in lowliness, asking for His help and His mercy. Women took part in these prayers with the men, that is, the people in all their groups, that God might protect them.

4.6.0.en: Sackcloth: coarse garments suited to austerity and humbling oneself before God. It was made of camel's hair or goat's hair, dark in color, and was worn either under the outer garments or over them, as a declaration of grief and humility before God.

4.6.1.en: The priests led the people in humbling themselves before God in prayer; they put on sackcloth, and so did the rest of the people, that is, they put aside the wearing of splendor, because of their sense of their weakness and to show their humility before God.

4.6.2.en: The people cast their children down before the temple of the Lord, declaring their inability to protect them and asking for His mercy and His deliverance of them and their children. Then we find an act we hear of for the first time, declaring the extent of grief and humility before God, when the priests covered the altar of bronze with sackcloth, offering their supplications and humility, they and their altar and all their sacrifices, seeking through them the mercy of God.

4.7.0.en: All the people and their leaders took part in praying and crying out to God, that He might have mercy on them and deliver their children, because they were weak, and likewise their women, from being seized by the enemies, who would divide them among themselves to lie with them. They also asked for the deliverance of their cities from the ruin of the enemies, and they made supplication above all for their holy temple, that the enemies might not enter it and defile it, and that God might protect them from shame and mockery among the nations, but lift them up and glorify them. This shows the extent of their faith in the power of God and at the same time their humility and their sense of their great need of the delivering hand of God. They differ from the rest of the nations, which feared Holofernes and surrendered in despair, because the fear of the Jews drove them in faith to make supplication to God and ask for His help, and they also did their duty in the preparation for war according to the commands of the high priest, so that in the end they obtained the power of God supporting them, as will appear in the following chapters.

4.7.1.en: The hour of affliction is the strongest moment in which fervent prayers go forth, in which a person humbles himself before God and casts all his hope upon Him, so that he feels the presence of God with him and enjoys His care.

4.8.s.en: (3) The encouragement of the high priest

4.8.0.en: Eliakim felt his responsibility for his people, as their spiritual and civil leader, so he went about through the lands of the children of Israel to encourage them to prepare and to face the enemies with faith.

4.9.0.en: He assured them that God would surely answer their requests if they persevered in their striving and their prayers, not because God does not hear them, but because their persistence shows their faith and their clinging to God and draws out His mercies.

4.10.0.en: He reminded them of the power of God who dwells in their midst, who had strengthened Moses the chief of the prophets in ancient times when he faced his enemies the Amalekites, who relied on their strength and their weapons, and defeated them, not with more weapons than those the people had, but by his prayers which he raised on the mountain, so that Joshua the commander of the army was able to defeat them, and God showed by this that it was His power that overcame the enemies and not the power of His people (Ex 17:8-13).

4.11.0.en: If God defeated the Amalekites, then you understand, O people of God, that He is able to defeat all enemies however great their strength, on condition that the people continue in their faith and their prayers. Thus, by practical proofs, Eliakim encouraged his people, so that they would not be dismayed at the power of the enemies and the submission of all to them.

4.11.1.en: Here the importance of the work of the servant appears, indeed the responsibility of each one of us in encouraging others and supporting them in their spiritual striving, whether with our brethren or our children, however great their apparent weakness or the strength of the problems that meet them. For God, who strengthened our holy fathers, is able to support us in all our steps, that we may triumph over all the wars of the devil, and prosper in everything our hands reach out to.

4.12.0.en: The people took courage, so they continued in prayer before the temple of the Lord and in every place, with supplications and faith in His power, leaving aside their comfort and their material needs in order to hold fast to fervent prayers before God.

4.13.0.en: The people came forward with repentance and many prayers, and offered sacrifices to God that He might have mercy on them. The priests and the Levites who offered the sacrifices did so in humility and with many prayers, wearing sackcloth and beseeching God to have mercy on them; indeed, to carry their humility further they put ashes on their heads, to declare that they were dust and ashes before God and that He was their only strength.

4.14.0.en: In sum, all were asking God to intervene, that He might preserve His people and protect them from the enemies and never leave them, because of their need of Him.

4.14.1.en: Perseverance in spiritual striving confirms our clinging to God and brings us His mercies, because perseverance is proof of our sonship, so we enjoy the care of God – our spiritual Father – and He brings us out of all our troubles. So we are not troubled if the spiritual striving is prolonged, for victory is guaranteed to us by God as long as we hold fast to Him.

4.14.2.en: We see in this chapter specific steps by which the people prepared for war, that is, their fear turned into practical striving, as follows:

4.14.3.en: 1- They built walls for the villages (v. 4).

4.14.4.en: 2- They gathered wheat in the cities (v. 4).

4.14.5.en: 3- They secured the ascents of the mountains (v. 6).

4.14.6.en: 4- They guarded the passages between the mountains (v. 6).

4.14.7.en: 5- They prayed to God with crying and supplication (v. 8).

4.14.9.en: 7- They humbled themselves by wearing sackcloth, the priests and the people and even the altar (v. 9).

4.14.10.en: 8- They cast their children down before God (v. 9).

4.14.11.en: 9- They asked for their women to be delivered from being seized (v. 10).

4.14.12.en: 10- They asked for the protection of their cities and their temple from ruin and defilement for the sake of the glory of God, so that they would not become a reproach (v. 10).

4.14.13.en: 11- The high priest went about encouraging the people and reminding them of the power of God which was with the fathers and that it would be with them (v. 11).

4.14.14.en: 12- They continued in prayers before God (v. 15).

4.14.15.en: 13- The priests and the Levites humbled themselves by putting ashes on their heads (v. 16). Achior informs Holofernes of the power of the children of Israel
